Targeted `go test` may fail on a read-only sandbox; then rely on the sealed evidence. Report every defect at once, classified blocker or follow-up.

Evidence references: the engine refuses a conclusion whose criterion cites a structural fact (an `SD-...` id) or a requirement id as its evidence. For design-causality and assumption-integrity cite the bundle's `structure:design-<id>` evidence; for the others cite the sealed `unit:`, `integration:`, `build:` or `e2e:` evidence ids listed in the bundle. Do not cite `SD-...`, `R<N>` or file paths as criterion evidence.

Plan tool classes: the plan tool `surface-check` requires evidence of both classes `integration` and `reachability`. In its tool disposition cite one sealed `integration:` evidence id and one sealed `reachability:` evidence id from the bundle (for example `reachability:pose-mcp/go/delivery-reachability` and `integration:pose-mcp/go/delivery-integration`), in addition to the result of running the tool. Check each tool's `evidence_classes` in the plan and cite every class it lists.

Latest corrections: the sealed-checkout marker now carries the checkout's path (a fixture or another root is not suppressed), and explicit ranges collect per-commit records so a data file created and moved into an administrative class stays material. If the full three-package test run fails only because your process inherits POSE_SEALED_CHECKOUT, unset it for that run.
